problems.field: outcomes[S1-O2,S1-O3,S1-O12,S1-O17].question; ai_available_when_produced; phase attributed to pooled reported results

form_value.shared_measure_detail: The treatment label denotes the original assisted condition; pooled plots are not consistently restricted to sessions 1-3, so their numbers must not be treated as verified phase-specific randomized estimates.

problems.source_says: AI availability is explicit for sessions 1-3 and for the two session-4 transitions, but the paper does not explicitly restrict Figures 16, 18, 19 or 21 to sessions 1-3 or identify the original/current-group composition of each aggregate. Original LLM returnees wrote without AI in session 4, whereas original Brain-only returnees used AI. Consequently these pooled results cannot be certified as exclusively with-AI/across-people results under the original-assignment arm labels used in the form. The form acknowledges this uncertainty in prose, but its categorical availability and question fields remain definite; phase-specific attribution of the pooled quantities is unconfirmed, not a demonstrated numerical error.
problems.quote: participants were assigned to the same group for the duration of sessions 1, 2, 3 but in case they decided to come back for session 4, they were reassigned to another group.
problems.locator: PDF p. 28, The session 4 prompts; p. 117, transition definitions; pp. 55-59, Figures 16, 18, 19 and 21; creativity-codebook.md, sections 1 and 6

problems.field: construct; question; measure_detail claim that the outcome concerns different writers

form_value.question: across_people
form_value.measure_detail_excerpt: This outcome concerns different writers; the same-writer session-change analysis is recorded separately.
form_value.computed_over: All essay pairs within each tool group, according to Fig. 19. Repeated essays per writer occur in the study; exclusion of within-writer pairs and separation by session are not stated for this heatmap.

problems.source_says: Figure 19 compares all essays within each group, and each writer contributed repeated essays. Neither its text nor its caption excludes pairs from the same writer; the displayed matrix also includes self-similarities on the diagonal. Thus a measure restricted to different people, as required by the codebook, is not established. Separately recording the within-writer Figure 12 analysis does not remove within-writer comparisons from Figure 19. The form correctly records the all-pairs caveat, but cannot simultaneously certify a purely across-people diversity measure from this heatmap.
problems.quote: We used the same LLM model to create embeddings for each essay, and then measured cosine distances between all essays within the same group.
problems.locator: PDF p. 57, paragraph above and caption of Figure 19; pp. 23 and 28, repeated-session protocol; creativity-codebook.md, section 6, diversity definition

problems.source_says: Figure 16 counts words and sentences, which supports elaboration and an output-level observation. The codebook defines category_count as counts of ideas, categories or unique ideas, not any numerical count. The form explicitly substitutes a generic count-based interpretation, which is not the supplied definition. No defined measure code for simple word/sentence length is confirmed; this needs an explicit coding-rule decision rather than treating category_count as source-supported.
problems.quote: The average length of the sentences and words per group can be seen in Figure 16 below.
problems.locator: PDF p. 55, Figure 16 and preceding sentence; creativity-codebook.md, section 6, Measure: category_count

problems.source_says: Figures 47-55 show session-4 ratings by both human teachers and the AI judge, with session and current tool group identified. The form separately codes only human-rated after-AI uniqueness (S1-O13). AI-rated uniqueness of LLM-to-Brain essays, and their content, language/style and structure/organization ratings by each assessor, have no corresponding after_ai entries. These are scored on unassisted essays after prior AI use and must use after_ai with AI availability no if retained. They are descriptive figure results, not controlled retention effects; numerical arm estimates remain unconfirmed. The notes acknowledge omitted follow-up combinations, but they are still absent from the outcome array.
problems.quote: Below we can see the z-score distribution of the assessments made by human teachers and AI judge based on metrics like uniqueness, content, language and style, structure and organization.
problems.locator: PDF p. 76, Scoring per topic; pp. 77-84, Figures 47-55 and legends (especially Figures 51 and 54, pp. 80 and 83, inspected directly); pp. 28 and 117, LLM-to-Brain protocol; creativity-codebook.md, section 1

problems.field: outcomes: missing AI language/style and human/AI accuracy ratings
problems.source_says: The output-rating displays include AI-judge Language and Style as well as Accuracy from both assessors. S1-O16 records only the teachers' language/style scores, and no outcome entry records either assessor's accuracy score. These bear on essay quality under the same usefulness rationale used for content and organization; accuracy here is an essay-quality rating, not a convergent creativity test. The plotted labels can be retained without guessing their mapping to Vocabulary/Grammar in the methods. The notes acknowledge these omissions, but do not provide coded outcomes. No overall treatment-effect numbers should be inferred from the rater-comparison prose.
problems.quote: accuracy mostly scored high (above 3.9) for both: teachers and the AI judge (Figure 44).
problems.locator: PDF pp. 72-75, evaluation methods, Figure 40 legend, Figure 41 and Figure 45 discussion; pp. 76-84, Language and Style in Figures 47-55; creativity-codebook.md, section 6

problems.source_says: The paper separately discusses variability of essay length/word counts across groups in Figure 15. S1-O12 records only average length from Figure 16. Figure 15 is relevant to homogenization of outputs and has printed group p-value labels LLM 0.39, Search Engine 0.02 and Brain Only 0.49, all checked directly. Its prose alternates between word length and number of words, and neither the test nor the tested null is specified; the labels cannot be treated as pairwise treatment-comparison p-values or as variances. This unresolved output-dispersion outcome appears only in the form notes, not in a coded outcome entry.
problems.quote: LLM and Search Engine groups had significantly smaller variability in the length of the words, compared to the Brain-only group, see Figure 15 below, which demonstrates p values of the words per group variability.
problems.locator: PDF p. 55, Quantitative statistical findings and Figure 15, including directly inspected bar labels; forms/c416.json, notes and S1-O12
